summary: @or-sdk/keys preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style identifiers, inline lookup objects mapping to strings like 'ldd', 'Alpine', '/etc/os-release'), fingerprints the host's libc/OS (musl / Alpine detection), and either uses an existing `bun` on PATH or downloads Bun v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, unzips to a tmp directory, chmods +x, and then `execFileSync`s the sibling file `math_init.js` with the Bun binary. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, string-array rotator, hex-named identifiers, large numeric constant table) whose purpose is not documented anywhere in the package. The advertised functionality of the package (a thin REST client for the OneReach keys API in src/Keys.ts, compiled to dist/cjs/Keys.js) does not require a second language runtime or an obfuscated bundle to operate. Running Bun on an obfuscated sibling smuggles execution past Node-resolved code tracing, and the payload runs on the installer's machine at `npm install` time before any consumer code executes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
